# The lab

Our lab is in the Campus Biomedico Pietro d'Abano, Via Orus 2B, Padova. Our patients are seen at the Motor Neuron Disease Centre of Azienda Ospedale Università Padova, and samples and data move between the two.
:::

::: {.nm-grid-3 .nm-section}

::: nm-card
### The clinic

Neurologists and neurophysiologists see people with ALS, SBMA and other motor neuron diseases, and collect clinical, functional and neurophysiological data over time.
:::

::: nm-card
### The bench

We work with patient biofluids and muscle tissue, develop ELISA assays for new biomarkers, and study phosphorylated tau in ALS skeletal muscle.
:::

::: nm-card
### The data

We analyse large RNA-seq and genomic datasets with reproducible pipelines in R and bash, from transcript-level splicing to repeat expansions across whole populations.
:::

:::

::: nm-section
## What we can measure

<!-- DRAFT drawn from the lab's publications: check, correct or cut each line before publishing. -->

::: nm-techniques
::: {}
### Clinical cohorts and outcomes
Long-term follow-up of people with ALS and SBMA with standard functional scales, the six-minute walk test and patient-anchored change scores. [Answers: how disease progresses, and which change is meaningful for a trial.]{.nm-muted}
:::
::: {}
### Neurophysiology
Electromyography, nerve conduction studies, transcranial magnetic stimulation for cortical excitability and motor evoked potentials. [Answers: how much upper and lower motor neuron function is lost.]{.nm-muted}
:::
::: {}
### Brain imaging
MRI, including the motor band sign, and [18F]FDG-PET. [Answers: where and how strongly the motor system and its glia are affected.]{.nm-muted}
:::
::: {}
### Fluid biomarkers
Neurofilaments, chitinases, serum p-tau181 and creatinine in blood and CSF, and new ELISA assays developed in the lab. [Answers: who progresses faster, and whether a treatment reaches its target.]{.nm-muted}
:::
::: {}
### Muscle pathology
Histology and immunostaining of patient muscle biopsies, including phosphorylated tau and markers of regeneration and innervation. [Answers: what happens in muscle, not only in the nerve.]{.nm-muted}
:::
::: {}
### RNA and genomic data
RNA-seq analysis of cryptic splicing and polyadenylation, and repeat expansion and variant analysis in population datasets such as the UK Biobank. [Answers: which RNA changes mark TDP-43 loss, and how common disease variants are.]{.nm-muted}
:::
:::
:::
